title: The one King Oliver recording date, July 1932
summary: Phillips recalls the Vocalion session for Sweet Like This and Mule-Faced Blues, its full personnel including Tiny Taylor and King Oliver on trumpet, and that nothing was released.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: This is Friday, the 28th, 1983. Yesterday we just finished saying something about the Young band, at the very end, but before that we were getting into King Oliver, and you were telling about Lester was in the band and he was so well accepted and everything. He had a lot of long solos, he had a lot of space and he would do a lot of showmanship type acts up on stage.
Yeah.
Some more questions about King Oliver. First of all, you said you did some recordings with him. You joined in May of '32, right?
April.
Anyway, did you do some recording dates? What about that?
Yeah, we made one date -- one recording date.
Phillips - 126
Do you remember when that was?
That must have been something like July of '32.
So Lester Young was not in there.
No, he wasn't.
This was before he joined.
Yeah.
Can you remember any of the things that were done, and any of the personnel?
We just made two takes, of "Sweet Like This" and "The Mule-Faced Blues."
Do you remember what label that was on?
Vocalion.
"Sweet Like This" and "Mule-Faced Blues" on Vocalion. Do you remember who was on that record?

Yes. Sam Allen and Francis Whitby and Jack Holt were the saxophone section. Sam Allen played first alto, Whitby played tenor, and Jack Holt played third alto. Arthur Williams, trumpet. Pete Jones, trombone. I was on the other trumpet. It had Eddie Anderson on bass horn -- tuba. Bernie Cobbs on guitar. Debo Mills on drums.
Dewitt Mills.
But we called him Debo. That's what everybody knew him in show business, by Debo. His name is Dewitt. And we had Charlie Toran on piano. And Tiny Taylor
Phillips - 127
was singing.
We've been through most of these names, but it's good to have them anyway.
And King Oliver.
On cornet or trumpet?
Trumpet. Everybody was playing trumpet then. So that was the band.
Incidentally, did he ever play any cornet when you were in the band, or was it always trumpet?
No, no. Trumpet.
He never played cornet when you were in the band.
No. He played the cornet back in the 20's. The Buescher people gave him a gold-plated trumpet, a special trumpet. They had it built for him, and they gave it to him.
I think we were talking about Buescher horns earlier, that Lester was playing them.
Yeah, he was a Buescher man.
At that time.
Yeah.
Later on he got into Conn.
Yeah. Then later, when he passed, he had a Selmer. The Selmer people gave him two when he went over to Paris.
Is there anyone else who was on that recording date with King Oliver?
Phillips - 128
No. That's all on that one.
Did that ever get released?
I don't think so.
Well, that will be something to look for. Because I don't think the '32 sides are well known.
Yeah.
Did you ever have any copies of it?
No.
I guess they didn't make any.
They didn't make none.
